text: V1 is scoped. Now the first real architecture decision: what actually runs this program. The cheap-looking answer is a shared spreadsheet of data owners -- and it's close to the reason this problem exists today.
A spreadsheet can't scan two million customer records across five systems, can't apply a classification label that actually protects a column, and its lineage stops at whatever tool wrote it.
The answer is Microsoft Purview: one governance domain, Veridian Data Governance, with all five systems registered and scanned in its Data Map -- one catalog, not five private spreadsheets.
This doesn't touch the five production systems themselves -- no migration, no downtime, no rebuilt reports. Purview connects to what already exists and catalogs it.
The platform is chosen. Next: registering the first real source in Purview's Data Map, and watching the first scan run.
